raw_response:
I have been working this land for fifty years. My father farmed before me. My wife and I eat from these 2 mu, and we sell what is left. I do not need anyone to tell me how to run my farm — I know this soil, I know this weather.

**My thinking:**

My land does the wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone in this village. Wheat goes in after October, maize goes in after wheat harvest in June. Same 2 mu, two crops a year.

For **wheat**, I buy improved seed from the village supply station — they sell the good variety, better than my saved seed from before. I put base fertilizer in when I till in autumn: compound fertilizer plus some extra urea. Then I topdress at jointing. I water four times — before winter freeze, at jointing, at heading, and once more before grain fills. I spray for aphids and do one herbicide pass. Rotary till in autumn, that is enough. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **maize**, I always use hybrid seed — I learned this twenty years ago, the yield difference is real. I apply fertilizer at planting and again when the plant is knee-high. I only water three times since summer has some rain, but my well is there if it is dry. One pesticide spray for armyworm, maybe one more if I see problems. I do not deep-plough — no need, the wheat roots loosened the soil. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

At my age, I keep things simple. I cannot carry as much as I used to, so I hire a neighbor's son for harvest.
